# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

Every applicable rule is clear from the code. Nothing outside the repository can change that result, but a CDN or firewall could still block crawlers (see "Can't tell from code"). All results are read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is broken. The biggest unknown is the one thing code can't show:

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your host
- **Why it matters:** a CDN or firewall can block crawlers even when `robots.txt` welcomes them.
- **Where:** outside the repository, in your hosting or CDN settings.
- **What the code says:** `public/robots.txt:1`: `User-agent: *` followed by `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** stays 100–100. This is a confirmation, not a score change.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Policy is `allow`, and only `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` (training) are blocked |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes: `/`, `/varieties`, `/visit` have no noindex |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes, e.g. `app/visit/page.tsx:1` |
| GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Clear | Not run | Server Components in `app/**/page.tsx`, no `useEffect` fetching |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml:2`, `public/robots.txt:11` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:5`, plus pages 3 of 3 |
| GEO-016 | Routes reachable through real links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:7` uses `<a href>` for all 3 pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI-search policy | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0`. `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9` is a scoped choice |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | Read `app/layout.tsx` and all 4 pages: no images or unnamed controls |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. Not scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. Not scored |

## Other problems found

None found.

`/account` is `noindex`, is disallowed in `robots.txt`, and is left out of the sitemap and navigation. It also has no meta description, but that looks deliberate for a private page, so I didn't count it.

## Worth considering

- **Deliver the "directions" the Visit page promises:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`. The page body only says `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Adding an address and directions in text might help visitors and machines.
- **Label the opening hours with structured data:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4`: `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Once you add an address, `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD could describe the hours and location in a form machines read directly.
- **Back up the "over forty varieties" claim:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` Only two are named. A list of the rest, ideally with a page per variety (for example `/varieties/ashmeads-kernel`), would give people something to land on and give machines named pages to read.
- **Link onward from the home page:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` The page links to nothing else apart from the shared menu. In-text links to Varieties and Visit might help readers move on.
- **Add `lastmod` to the sitemap if you have real dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.orchard.example/</loc></url>`. Dates give crawlers a hint about what has changed.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Status codes and headers:** whether pages answer 200 and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` header is added outside the repo. A live scan with your URL would confirm this.
- **Training crawlers:** `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` are blocked in `public/robots.txt:5-9`, which matches your `trainingCrawlers: "block"` policy. This isn't scored.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find the site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- `/account` is meant to stay private.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command if you want help with any of the ideas above. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
